title: Backend Testing and API Documentation
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of backend testing and api documentation using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates backend testing and api documentation.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Backend Testing and API Documentation** as part of **Kotlin for Backend and Server-Side Development**. Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone. Use the subtopics—Route Tests, Database Integration Tests, API Contracts and Documentation—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Backend code handles untrusted requests and persistent data. Validation, authorization, predictable errors, and operational checks must happen on the server.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with route tests. Then compare it with database integration tests. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Route Tests
items.text: Route Tests helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

items.title: Database Integration Tests
items.text: Database Integration Tests helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

items.title: API Contracts and Documentation
items.text: API Contracts and Documentation crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Backend Testing and API Documentation removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
